comparison: Perfect agreement on background claims (C2, C34, C89, C91) about established field effectiveness of push-pull systems. Both evaluations find these literature-based claims well-supported without concerns.

Strong agreement on volatile detection methodology and findings (C6, C7, C44-C49, C72, C74-C75, C90). Both find the GC-MS analysis and identification of compounds well-supported. OpenEval includes additional claims (C100) not mentioned in peer review.

Complete agreement on no-choice assay results (C64-C67, C86-C87). Both evaluations find these findings supported by adequate experimental data and methodology. OpenEval includes C88 not explicitly mentioned in peer review.

Significant disagreement on dual-choice flight tunnel results (C11-C12, C57-C63). OpenEval rates as UNCERTAIN due to lack of statistical significance and methodological limitations (C103-C104), while peer reviewers implicitly accept these findings as SUPPORTED without raising concerns.

Agreement on cage oviposition assay results (C9, C53-C56, C77-C78). Both find strong support for preference findings with adequate statistical evidence. Peer review also includes C10, C81-C82 which OpenEval addresses separately in R3.

Partial overlap on indirect contact oviposition results (C10, C81-C82). OpenEval rates as SUPPORTED but notes critical methodological limitations about distance and volatile gradients. Peer review groups these with C9 findings and accepts without specific concern about limitations.

Agreement on overall conclusions (C13, C68-C70, C15). Both evaluations find the authors' cautious interpretation appropriate given mixed results. OpenEval emphasizes the fair assessment of data; peer reviewers praise the transparent and nuanced conclusions. Peer review also includes C14, C71.

Agreement on methodological limitations documentation (C76). Both evaluations view transparent acknowledgment of limitations positively. OpenEval addresses broader limitation claims (C96-C99); peer review focuses on C76, C102-C104 as contributing to study credibility.

Minimal overlap on speculative alternative mechanisms (C71). OpenEval rates C71, C84-C85, C92-C93 as UNCERTAIN since they represent untested hypotheses. Peer review groups C71 with overall conclusions and accepts the discussion as appropriate without distinguishing speculation from findings.

OpenEval evaluates literature review claims (C3-C5, C38-C42) about conflicting findings as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; these background claims were likely accepted implicitly.
OpenEval evaluates contextual claims about volatile compounds (C50-C52) as SUPPORTED by appropriate citations. No corresponding peer review evaluation found.
OpenEval evaluates inference about cited study design (C80) as SUPPORTED. No corresponding peer review evaluation found; this interpretive claim was not specifically addressed by reviewers.
OpenEval rates DEET exposure confound (C105-C106) as UNCERTAIN due to unknown effects on lepidopterans despite mitigation efforts. Peer reviewers did not raise this as a concern.

Peer review explicitly commends acknowledgment of limitations (C76, C102-C104) as contributing to credibility. OpenEval addresses these across multiple results (R3, R8) with more granular evaluation of specific limitation types.
